what_worked: Rollout 0's SQL scan of episodes between 73590 and 73800 did correctly surface the right 30-second/3-minute episode rows covering the true chest-opening event, showing that direct time-window SQL scanning near a plausible boss time can succeed where name-based semantic search fails.

Multiple rollouts correctly used clip_qa to attempt to read on-screen loot notification text rather than relying purely on possibly-absent structured captions, which is the right general strategy for numeric HUD values.
transferable_lessons: When a question names an entity that doesn't exactly match any DB entity string, do not trust the single top semantic_search hit as boss identity; cross-check against the entities table for all names containing the key characters/gloss (e.g. 金睛/golden-eyed) and prefer entities explicitly typed as 'boss:' over generic action descriptions.

For 'last X before boss Y' questions, first pin down boss Y's time window precisely via the entities table (first_seen_s/last_seen_s), then scan backward through episodes/object_states for the nearest preceding chest -- don't accept the first 'golden beast'-sounding boss match from semantic search.

When calling clip_qa around a suspected item-pickup/HUD-number event, widen the window a few seconds past the visually obvious action (e.g. past the chest-opening animation) since pickup notification banners with numbers often render slightly after the interaction, not during it; a 'no number visible' clip_qa result close to a window boundary should trigger a follow-up call with an expanded window rather than being accepted as ground truth of zero/absence.

Do not let clip_qa's yes/no identity-confirmation answers override structured entity time bounds already found elsewhere (e.g. the entities table); treat visual identity confirmations of a boss fight as lower-confidence than a matching named entity row with the same time range.

If a later, higher-quality retrieval hit (matching the full question phrasing) surfaces a different/better candidate window than the one currently being investigated, re-anchor on it rather than continuing to verify the earlier candidate.
